Oral Order
4 07-08-2025 Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the State.

2. The present Memo of Appeal has been preferred against the judgment of conviction dated 04-03-2025 and order sentence dated 06-03-2025 passed by learned Additional & Sessions Judge-XXI, Patna in Sessions Trial No. 253 of 2023 arising out of Shastri Nagar P.S. Case No.
553/2022 under sections 489(A), 489(B), 489(C), 420, 417, 120(B), 418, 419 of the Indian Penal Code.
He has been convicted under Section- 489(B) r/w 120(B) and 489(C) of the Indian Penal Code.

He has been awarded rigorous imprisonment of seven years with a fine of Rs. 10,000/-
(Rupees Ten thousand only).
Further R. I. five years with a fine of Rs. 5,000/- for offence under Section- Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.1456 of 2025(4) dt.07-08-2025 489(c) of the Indian Penal Code and in default of payment of fine, an additional S.I. for six months.
Both the sentences are directed to run concurrently.
3. As per allegation, on a secret information, the police reached at the place of occurrence and apprehended two accused persons including the appellant.
On search, fake currency notes were recovered from their possession.

sentences.text: While making the prayer to suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellant, learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the prosecution has not proved its case beyond shadow of reasonable doubts.
The appellant has falsely been implicated in the present case.
It has also been submitted that neither any fake currency was recovered nor any incriminating material was found from his conscious possession.
It has also been submitted that the appellant has no concern with the alleged recovered fake currency.
The appellant is in custody since 01-09-2022 and there is no likelihood of the appeal being taken up for hearing in near future.
5. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant by submitting that there is recovery of fake currency notes from possession of the appellant.
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1456 of 2025(4) dt.07-08-2025 6.

Considering the above-mentioned facts and circumstances and also the fact that there is recovery of fake currency notes from possession of the appellant, presently I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail and accordingly, the same is rejected.
7. However, the appellant will be at liberty to renew his prayer for bail after serving half of the sentence.

(Nawneet Kumar Pandey, J) kundan/-
